subject.title: Compaction should use auth-profile rotation / failover within the same provider

question: Should compaction adopt same-provider auth-profile failover using the linked PR's auto-only, user-lock-preserving, stable-transcript retry design?
rationale: Repository policy treats fallback/auth/session-state behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and the issue discussion specifically calls out the risk of duplicate summaries or stale transcript compaction if retries are not bounded.

options.title: Review and land guarded failover
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR or an equivalent fix only if it preserves user-locked profiles and proves apply-once retry behavior against a stable transcript snapshot.

options.title: Narrow the PR first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask the PR author to reduce the fix to the minimum compaction-auth path and stronger idempotency proof before merge.

options.title: Postpone compaction failover
options.body: Keep current compaction strictness and document the limitation until maintainers choose a broader fallback policy.

recommendation.title: Review and land guarded failover
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR or an equivalent fix only if it preserves user-locked profiles and proves apply-once retry behavior against a stable transcript snapshot.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent native/context-engine compaction work makes joshavant the best available routing candidate for the compaction retry semantics decision.
